name: Canakinumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 4 or 8 weeks; single doses for gout flares

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1κ antibody against IL-1β, generated in transgenic mice. Year of first patent filing (priority August 2000, Novartis, US 7,446,175).

tagline: Long-acting anti-IL-1β antibody for periodic fever syndromes and Still's disease
summary: Canakinumab is a human monoclonal antibody that neutralises interleukin-1β. It is used for rare autoinflammatory periodic fever syndromes, Still's disease and gout flares, and was the subject of CANTOS, the first trial to show that targeting inflammation reduces cardiovascular events.
mechanism: Canakinumab binds IL-1β with high affinity and prevents it from interacting with the IL-1 receptor, without affecting IL-1α or the natural antagonist IL-1Ra.

In cryopyrinopathies, gain-of-function NLRP3 mutations cause excess inflammasome activation and IL-1β release; neutralising IL-1β suppresses fever, rash, arthritis and the acute-phase response. Its long half-life allows dosing every 4–8 weeks.
uses: Still's disease (adult-onset and systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis)
Gout flares when NSAIDs and colchicine are unsuitable

history.title: FDA and EU approval
history.detail: Approved in June (US) and October (EU) for cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes.

history.title: Systemic JIA
history.detail: Approved for systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis.

history.title: Periodic fevers
history.detail: FDA approves it for TRAPS, HIDS/MKD and FMF.

history.title: CANTOS
history.detail: Canakinumab reduces recurrent cardiovascular events and lung cancer incidence; Novartis does not obtain a cardiovascular indication.

history.title: Adult-onset Still's disease
history.detail: FDA approves canakinumab for active Still's disease including AOSD.

history.title: Gout flares
history.detail: FDA approves it for gout flares in adults who cannot use NSAIDs or colchicine.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: CANTOS (2017) enrolled over 10,000 patients and provided the first proof that anti-inflammatory therapy alone reduces cardiovascular events.
Fatal infections were more frequent with canakinumab in CANTOS.
